# Puṇṇapātijātaka (Ja 53)
**ID:** Ja 53
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Puṇṇapātijātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja53

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Puṇṇapātijātaka* (Ja 53) is a short narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In the standard edition of the *Jātakaṭṭhakathā*, it appears as the third story of its vagga, opening with the verse line *Tatheva puṇṇapātiyo ti* [Fausböll 1877].
The background narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana near Sāvatthi and concerns drugged liquor (*visavāruṇī*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. A band of impoverished rogues concocted a plot to drug and rob the wealthy householder Anāthapiṇḍika by inviting him to drink spirits [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Fausböll 1877]. Anāthapiṇḍika initially declined on his way to see the king; on his return, noticing that the drink stood completely untouched and full (*puṇṇapātiyo*), he astutely deduced that the sellers would not leave their own brew untasted unless it were poisoned, and boldly confronted the swindlers, causing them to flee in fear [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Fausböll 1877]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the swindlers were the same rogues from the past, while he himself had been the wise merchant of Bārāṇasī (*Bārāṇasiseṭṭhi*) who outsmarted them in a former life [Fausböll 1877].
Neither SuttaCentral nor the automated text-matching of DharmaNexus identifies any Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan for this Jātaka [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
